To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) melt inclusions trapped within olivine crystals from the 1790-2018 CE eruptions of Kīlaueau volcano, Hawai’i, record the storage and remobilisation of crystal cargoes from magmatic mush piles; (2) melt inclusions from the same eruption exhibit extreme compositional variability, reflecting the accumulation of inclusion-rich crystals over timescales of >170 years; and (3) melt inclusions are unsuitable for the investigation of carrier melt processes

melt inclusions in olivine crystals from Kīlaueva Volcano, Hawaiʻi, exhibit extreme compositional variability that exceeds that of all erupted lava compositions since the 1790s, and that the inclusion-bearing crystals were stored and remobilized from magmatic mush piles for >170 years.

melt inclusions trapped within primitive olivine cargoes display a high degree and wide range of geochemical disequilbria with their carrier melts, and that the melt inclusion populations trapped in primitive olives from a given eruption are more diverse than the lava compositions erupted over the past two centuries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how crystals and their inclusions become associated with erupting melts.
how crystals and their melt inclusion cargoes are transported and stored in magmatic systems.
the evolution of magmatic systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the melt inclusions are not representative of their carrier melts, which is not a surprise.
melt inclusion records of magmatic processes should not be taken for granted, and that they should be carefully scrutinized for evidence of disequilibrium with carrier melts.
the melt inclusions from the Kīlaueas volcano do not record the pre-eruption storage and processing of their host melts, but they do provide evidence that magmatic systems are mush dominated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

olivine-hosted melt inclusion records are not suitable for the investigation into eruption-specific processes, but they do record the long-term history of crystal storage and re-mobilization within magmatich mush piles.
melt inclusions are not a direct record of their carrier melt, but rather a record of their carrier crystal, which may have resided in a magmatic mush pile for hundreds of years before eruption.
the assumption of simple associations between olivines and their carrier melts is not always justified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
melt inclusion compositions can be used to infer the timescales of magmatic storage and remobilisation of crystal cargoes within mush zones.
melt inclusions are not always representative of the magmas they were erupted with, and that the assumption of simple melt inclusion-carrier melt associations is not always valid.

melt inclusion records of crystal accumulation and processing in mush zones are not limited to crystal-rich, crystal mush-dominated systems, but can be recorded in crystal-poor, crystal mush-dominated magmas.
